strings.name: Isabel Allende
strings.summary: Born in Peru, Allende grew up in Chile and worked in journalism before moving to Venezuela during military rule and later settling in the United States. Writing in Spanish, she interweaves family memory, women’s experiences and Latin American history in works including The House of the Spirits. Her fiction and memoirs circulate across languages. A foundation honoring her daughter supports women and girls, while she continues publishing new work.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through May 2025. The English translation and Spanish edition of the 2025 novel appeared on different dates in May; the translation date is not treated as the original-language publication date. Checked on 13 November 2026.
strings.influence.rationale: Through novels such as The House of the Spirits, she connects family narratives with Latin American history, builds a readership across languages and supports women’s rights.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f2.label: Early education
strings.facts.f2.value: Attended schools in Bolivia and Lebanon before returning to Chile to complete secondary school
strings.highlights.h1.title: Fiction across languages
strings.highlights.h1.text: The House of the Spirits linked family narrative with political history and launched her international career as a novelist.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Women’s and girls’ rights
strings.highlights.h2.text: Established the Isabel Allende Foundation in 1996 in memory of her daughter Paula to support related charitable programs.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Publishes a new historical novel
strings.timeline.t1.text: My Name Is Emilia del Valle explores nineteenth-century Chilean civil war through a woman war correspondent.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Receives Chile’s National Literature Prize
strings.timeline.t2.text: Received Chile’s National Literature Prize for a body of work engaging women, memory and Latin American history.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Establishes a foundation honoring her daughter
strings.timeline.t3.text: Created the Isabel Allende Foundation, turning remembrance of Paula into charitable support for women and children.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Publishes Paula
strings.timeline.t4.text: Published a memoir shaped by her daughter’s illness and death, connecting personal grief with family memory.
strings.timeline.t5.title: The House of the Spirits appears
strings.timeline.t5.text: Published her first novel while living in Venezuela, intertwining a family’s story with Latin American political history.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Moves to Venezuela
strings.timeline.t6.text: Left Chile with her family during military dictatorship and lived in Venezuela for thirteen years.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Joins Paula magazine
strings.timeline.t7.text: Began working for the women’s magazine Paula, writing reports, interviews and a humor column.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Born in Lima
strings.timeline.t8.text: Born while her father served as a Chilean diplomat; returned to Chile with her mother as a child and later attended schools abroad through family diplomatic postings.
